### Primary Question:Is the FAO transcriptional program in breast cancer predominantly associated with malignant cells, and does it differ across breast-cancer subtypes?

### Q1:Which cell populations have the strongest FAO scores: malignant cells, macrophages, other myeloid cells, or T cells?

```{python}
import scanpy as sc
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy.stats import kruskal
```

```{python}
adata = sc.read_h5ad("wu2021_brca.h5ad")   # log-normalized
```

```{python}
# Patients per subtype
pt_sub = adata.obs.groupby("orig.ident")["subtype"].first()
print(pt_sub.value_counts())
```

```{python}
# FAO score per cell
fao_genes = pd.read_csv("fao_genes.csv")["gene"].tolist()
fao_genes = [g for g in fao_genes if g in adata.var_names]
print("FAO genes found:", len(fao_genes))
sc.tl.score_genes(adata, fao_genes, score_name="FAO_score")
```

```{python}
# --- SQ1: FAO by cell type, per patient mean (all 26) ---
min_cells = 20
g = adata.obs.groupby(["orig.ident", "celltype_major"])["FAO_score"]
pt_ct = pd.concat([g.mean().rename("FAO"), g.size().rename("n")], axis=1).reset_index()
pt_ct = pt_ct[pt_ct["n"] >= min_cells]            # drop tiny groups
pt_ct["subtype"] = pt_ct["orig.ident"].map(pt_sub)

print(pt_ct.groupby("celltype_major")["FAO"].agg(["median", "count"]).round(3)
      .sort_values("median", ascending=False))
```

epithelial cells carry the FAO program, and malignant cells keep a modest share of it.

epithelial cells (normal and malignant) \> myeloid, CAFs and others \> T cells and B cells. Macrophages and myeloid cells are not the source.

```{python}
# --- Subtype question: malignant cells only ---
mal = pt_ct[pt_ct["celltype_major"] == "Cancer Epithelial"]
print(mal.groupby("subtype")["FAO"].agg(["median", "count"]).round(3))

groups = [d["FAO"].values for _, d in mal.groupby("subtype")]
if all(len(x) >= 2 for x in groups):
    print("Kruskal-Wallis p =", round(kruskal(*groups).pvalue, 3))
```

No FAO difference between subtypes in malignant cells.

```{python}
# Plots
fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(12, 4))
pt_ct.boxplot(column="FAO", by="celltype_major", ax=ax[0], rot=90)
mal.boxplot(column="FAO", by="subtype", ax=ax[1])
plt.tight_layout(); plt.savefig("fao_celltype_subtype.png", dpi=200)
plt.show()
#pt_ct.to_csv("fao_per_patient_celltype.csv", index=False)
```

### Q2:**Is malignant FAO associated with macrophage or CD8 abundance?**

```{python}
# Malignant-cell FAO per patient (>= 20 cancer cells)
cancer = adata.obs[adata.obs["celltype_major"] == "Cancer Epithelial"]
n = cancer.groupby("orig.ident").size()
fao_mal = cancer.groupby("orig.ident")["FAO_score"].mean()[n >= 20]
```

```{python}
from scipy.stats import spearmanr

# Immune abundance as a fraction of NON-epithelial cells,
# so tumor purity doesn't drive the number
nonepi = adata.obs[~adata.obs["celltype_major"].isin(
    ["Cancer Epithelial", "Normal Epithelial"])]
props = (nonepi.groupby(["orig.ident", "celltype_minor"]).size()
         .unstack(fill_value=0))
props = props.div(props.sum(axis=1), axis=0)

df = pd.DataFrame({"FAO_malignant": fao_mal,
                   "Macrophage": props["Macrophage"],
                   "CD8": props["T cells CD8+"]}).dropna()
df["subtype"] = adata.obs.groupby("orig.ident")["subtype"].first()
print(df.round(3))

def corr(d, label):
    for col in ["Macrophage", "CD8"]:
        rho, p = spearmanr(d["FAO_malignant"], d[col])
        print(f"{label}: FAO vs {col}: rho={rho:.2f}, p={p:.3f}, n={len(d)}")

corr(df, "All")
corr(df[df["subtype"] == "TNBC"], "TNBC only")
df.to_csv("fao_vs_immune_per_patient.csv")
```

The association is not detectable in this dataset, because the sample is too small to tell.
